subject: Dedicated pool headroom deficit — CEO note and action items
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@clearbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High error rate and queueing on our reserved pool

Rishi —

We started seeing sustained 5xx spikes and long tail latency this morning around 07:30 UTC. Our dashboards show queue depth backing up in the reserved GPU pool and requests falling back to lower-tier models (we're seeing increased cost and poorer quality). Key impacts:
- ~8% 5xx rate over last 45m (spike to 12% at 08:20)
- P95 latency increased from ~220ms -> 1.4s for generation routes
- Customers on our side are reporting timeouts on inference calls (payment risk).

We opened a ticket with support but wanted you in the loop — this is affecting our production traffic and the account is asking for immediate attention. Do you have an ETA on mitigation?

Attached a short error sample and a screenshot of the queue chart.

— Sam
ClearBridge (ops@clearbridge.com)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and queueing on our reserved pool

Team —

On Fri, Aug 28, 2027 at 09:12 AM Sam Patel <sam@clearbridge.com> wrote:
> Rishi —
> 
> We started seeing sustained 5xx spikes and long tail latency this morning...

Short summary: ClearBridge (RBW-DEAL-4831) is experiencing reserved-capacity queueing and elevated 5xx. This looks like dedicated pool headroom exhaustion: the reserved instances hit token/backlog contention and automatic routing dropped to fallback models. Customer is seeing both latency and correctness regressions.

Immediate asks:
1) David — can you confirm current reserved pool utilization, active jobs pinned to ClearBridge, and whether any noisy neighbor or migration pushed utilization over threshold? Attach the per-GPU inflight count and kernel error logs. ETA 30m.
2) Naomi — spin up a prioritized burst lane for this reservation (if auto-burst is available) and prepare the rollback policy to pin them to the previous model variant that has lower memory/KV usage. I need an ETA for conditional burst authorization.
3) Marissa — coordinate with the ClearBridge contact and let them know we are escalating to engineering and can offer short-term burst/credits if needed. Be explicit about expected time to reduce 5xx.
4) Aditya — I want the exec loop alerted if we cannot stabilize within 3 hours; please prep a 1-slide brief for CEO/CTO if needed.

I've attached the error sample Sam sent. I'll follow this thread with engineering notes once David returns GPU-level metrics.

— Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@clearbridge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-28T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and queueing on our reserved pool

Sam —

Thanks for flagging and for the sample logs. Quick updates from our side:
- Engineering has confirmed the reservation is consuming 96% of committed slots during peak windows and we observed a sustained burst at ~08:10–08:45 UTC consistent with a batch job from another tenant (noisy neighbor).
- We've opened a controlled burst for ClearBridge as an emergency short-term relief (prioritized traffic lane) — this should reduce queue depth within ~12–20 minutes after routing completes.
- In parallel, we're preparing a rollback to the lower-KV model variant for your routes to reduce per-request memory and improve P95. That rollback is expected to take ~45 minutes to validate.

What we are doing for you right now:
- Emergency burst enabled (priority lane) — monitor should show queue depth dropping;
- If that doesn't stabilize, we'll perform a validated rollback to the compatible model variant during a coordination window at 16:30 UTC;
- We will issue a small account credit for the disruption (discussing amount with finance).

I'll remain on this thread and send an update in 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we'll own the escalation and keep the lines open.

Best,
Marissa Coleman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-08-29T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mortem summary and exec note — ClearBridge reserved capacity event (RBW-DEAL-4831)

Team and stakeholders —

Final readout for the ClearBridge incident (timeline condensed):
- 2027-08-28 07:30 UTC: ClearBridge reports latency and 5xx; queue depth rising.
- 07:55–08:45 UTC: Noisy neighbor batch load caused reserved pool headroom to reduce to <4%. Autoscaling did not trigger due to a mix of pinned reservations and admission controls.
- 08:12 UTC: ClearBridge saw P95 jump to 1.4s and 5xx spike to 12%.
- 09:05 UTC: Emergency prioritized burst lane engaged (short-term relief). Queue depth reduced within 18 minutes.
- 09:50 UTC: Validated rollback to lower-KV model completed; 5xx dropped to baseline (0.6%) and latency returned near normal within ~30 minutes.

Root cause: A cross-tenant batch job created transient GPU headroom depletion in a dedicated cluster zone. Admission control prevented autoscale due to reservation gating. Our telemetry did not surface the kernel-level contention quickly enough because of an aggregation gap in the headroom alerts.

Actions completed:
- Emergency burst lane enabled and validated (Naomi).
- Rollback to lower-KV model for ClearBridge (David).
- Customer notification and credit commitment (Marissa).

Follow-up actions (owners & due dates):
1) Short-term (24–72h) — Naomi: Enable finer-grained headroom alerts per-reservation (threshold at 10% remaining) and a fast-path for automated conditional burst (due 2027-08-31).
2) Medium-term (2 weeks) — David & SRE: Harden admission control logic to allow conditional autoscale override when SLAs at risk; provide a safe throttle for noisy tenants (due 2027-09-12).
3) Product (Aditya): Review reservation policy and UI to surface per-reservation queue depth and top noisy processes (due 2027-09-05).
4) Exec communication (Rishi): Draft a one-slide summary for CEO/CTO and the ClearBridge execs detailing mitigation steps and credit. (sent separately to leadership).

Attachments included: clearbridge_error_sample.log, queue_depth-trend-aug28.png, reserved-capacity-runbook-v2.pdf

If we miss the short-term alerting delivery, escalate immediately to exec (Aditya and I will loop in CTO). This incident will inform the reserved-capacity hardening sprint next quarter.

— Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
